answer_text:
Let

\[
V_d = H^0(\mathbb{P}^n,\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^n}(d))
\]

be the vector space of homogeneous polynomials of degree \(d\) in \(n+1\) variables. Its dimension is the number of monomials of degree \(d\):

\[
\dim V_d=\binom{d+n}{d}.
\]

Thus the parameter space of degree \(d\) hypersurfaces in \(\mathbb{P}^n\) is

\[
\mathbb{P}(V_d)\cong \mathbb{P}^{\binom{d+n}{d}-1}.
\]

Now fix a point \(p\in \mathbb{P}^n\). The condition that a degree \(d\) hypersurface contain \(p\) is simply

\[
F(p)=0,
\]

which is a single linear condition on the coefficients of \(F\). In the parameter space \(\mathbb{P}^{\binom{d+n}{d}-1}\), this is a hyperplane.

For a generic set of

\[
m=\binom{d+n}{d}-1
\]

points, these \(m\) linear conditions are independent. Therefore the intersection of the corresponding \(m\) hyperplanes in

\[
\mathbb{P}^{\binom{d+n}{d}-1}
\]

has projective dimension

\[
\left(\binom{d+n}{d}-1\right)-\left(\binom{d+n}{d}-1\right)=0.
\]

A zero-dimensional projective space consists of exactly one point, so there is exactly one degree \(d\) hypersurface containing such a generic set of points.

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
